text: On the day she was crowned queen, Victoria rushed home to give her dog a bath.
Princess Victoria had a lonely childhood. Her closest friend was a spaniel called Dash.
She dressed him in a scarlet jacket and blue trousers.
For Christmas, she gave him rubber balls and two pieces of gingerbread.
He even had his portrait painted by Landseer, England's top animal painter.
Once, when she sailed off without him, Dash jumped into the sea and swam after her.
In eighteen thirty-eight, at nineteen, she was crowned.
It went badly. The ring was made for the wrong finger, and a bishop skipped two pages.
Then the new queen hurried back to the palace, ran upstairs, and gave Dash his bath.
Everyone wanted something from the queen. Dash just wanted his bath.
His gravestone reads: his attachment was without selfishness, his fidelity without deceit.
If you're missing a friend like that, talk to Jenny on Feeloy. She's always glad you're home.
